extracted.intended_audience: empirical researchers, economists, and policy analysts studying causal effects of patents on startups (and readers interested in econometric identification strategies using USPTO data)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and empirical validation strategy for identifying causal effects of patent grants on startup outcomes using examiner leniency as an instrument; covers instrument construction, validity checks, outcome measures, robustness tests, and interpretation of IV estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner leniency as an instrument (prior approval rate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an examiner’s prior approval rate (percent of reviewed applications she previously granted) as an instrument for whether a startup’s application is approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct the instrument excluding the focal application from numerator and denominator; alternative codings include leave-one-out estimators, using only the last three years, or approval rate of first-time applications. Report the first-stage coefficient (e.g., each percentage-point increase in prior approval rate raises grant probability by X) and ensure strong predictive power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance condition (first-stage strength)
rubrics_metrics.description: The instrument must strongly predict the endogenous treatment (whether the application is approved).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show a statistically strong first-stage (coefficient estimates and p-values) and report first-stage F-statistics well above the rule-of-thumb value of 10 to avoid weak-instrument bias. Report point estimates of first-stage effect size (e.g., 0.67 percentage-point increase in approval probability per percentage-point of examiner prior approval rate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion restriction and quasi-random assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Argue and test that examiner leniency affects startup outcomes only through patent approval, relying on quasi-random assignment of applications to examiners at the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide institutional explanation of assignment mechanisms (e.g., serial-number last-digit, FIFO) and cite prior literature. Discuss plausibility of exclusion restriction and potential threats (e.g., assignment correlated with application/applicant/examiner characteristics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation test of quasi-random assignment (Righi and Simcoe style)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under quasi-random assignment, the first-stage coefficient on the instrument should be invariant to including controls for application, applicant, and examiner characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate first stage with progressively richer controls; show coefficient stability across specifications. Include proxies for applicant quality (log employees, log sales, growth), application quality (log independent claims), examiner specialization, experience, and seniority. Use subclass-by-year or art-unit-by-year fixed effects as suggested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test for correlation between instrument and observed characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether examiner leniency correlates with observed drivers of startup success (applicant characteristics, application characteristics, examiner characteristics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report regressions of leniency on applicant size/growth, independent claims, examiner experience/seniority, workload, etc. If correlations exist (e.g., more senior examiners are more lenient), test whether these relationships invalidate identification via additional controls and robustness checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placebo and external-validity checks using foreign patent grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Use foreign patent grants as an alternative measure of application or invention quality and test whether assignment to lenient U.S. examiners is correlated with foreign grant outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If leniency is uncorrelated with foreign grant success, this supports the quasi-random-assignment/exclusion assumption. Report placebo regressions and their interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument robustness: sample cutoffs and alternative constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure instrument robustness to alternative sample selections and instrument definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: exclude examiners with fewer than 10 prior reviews (or try alternative cutoffs), recompute instrument using different windows (all first-time apps, last three years), and report that main results are robust to these choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model choice for first stage (linear probability vs probit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer a linear-probability model for the first-stage to avoid using nonlinearity as an extra identifying assumption, but check robustness with probit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate 2SLS first-stage with linear probability model; note Angrist & Pischke recommendation. Report that conclusions are robust to estimating the first-stage with probit as a sensitivity check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control for review speed as a potential confound
rubrics_metrics.description: Review speed (time from filing to first-action) may be correlated with examiner leniency and independently affect firm outcomes, so it must be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instrument review speed using administrative delays: decompose total time into filing-to-assignment (quasi-random admin delays) plus examiner’s average docket-to-first-action time. Include instrumented review speed as a control and show point estimates remain within confidence intervals of baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed-effects strategy to control for technological and regional heterogeneity
rubrics_metrics.description: Include fixed effects to absorb unobserved time-varying technology and location factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baseline includes art-unit-by-year and headquarter-state fixed effects. Additional specifications may include technology-subclass-by-year fixed effects or art-unit-by-application-year fixed effects (useful for IPO timing/censoring).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome measures for firm growth and survival
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and measure the primary firm-level outcomes impacted by patent approval: employment growth, sales growth, and firm survival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure effects at multiple horizons (1–5 years), report cumulative and year-by-year effects, visualize trajectories (e.g., Figure 2). Use NETS database to code survival and spot-check firm-death coding with Capital IQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures for follow-on innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Capture a firm’s subsequent inventive activity using several patent-based outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use log number of subsequent patent applications filed after first-action, log number subsequently approved, approval rate of subsequent applications, log total citations to subsequent applications, and log average citations per subsequent approved patent. Report percent changes and statistical significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heterogeneous-effects analysis (first vs later patents, sectoral differences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine whether effects differ between a startup’s first, second, and third patent applications and across sectors (e.g., IT startups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate separate 2SLS models for each application number and sector; report that first patent has large effects on growth and follow-on innovation while later patents affect mainly follow-on innovation. For IT sector, compare against survey literature and interpret mechanisms (licensing, bargaining chips, defensive uses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of IV estimates as LATE and discussion of external validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that IV/2SLS identifies a local average treatment effect (LATE) for compliers—startups whose grant status is affected by examiner leniency—and not necessarily the average treatment effect (ATE) for all startups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain who are never-takers, always-takers, and compliers (middling-quality applications). Discuss monotonicity (no defiers) and implications: LATE likely larger than ATE; compare 2SLS and OLS and explain selection bias intuition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting OLS counterparts and comparing estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Present OLS estimates alongside 2SLS to aid interpretation and illustrate selection bias and LATE vs ATE differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report OLS in appendix and discuss why OLS may be upwardly biased (positive selection into patentability) and why 2SLS estimates can be larger than OLS if compliers benefit more than average.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner-characteristics data and controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect and use data on examiner experience, seniority, specialization, and workload to test correlations with leniency and as robustness controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain examiner experience/seniority via FOIA if needed. Include these controls in first-stage and second-stage specifications and report whether inclusion affects estimated instrument coefficient (it should not if assignment is quasi-random).

rubrics_metrics.name: Placebo timing and falsification exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Run placebo tests (e.g., whether foreign grants predict assignment) to detect spurious instrument–outcome links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report placebo regression results that show no evidence of correlation, strengthening identification claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction detail: exclude focal application from instrument calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: When computing an examiner’s prior approval rate, neither the numerator nor denominator should include the focal application since it has not been reviewed prior to the measurement date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State this explicitly and verify robustness to alternative codings. This avoids mechanical bias in the instrument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling right-censoring for long-horizon outcomes (IPOs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address sample censoring for long-horizon outcomes (e.g., IPOs) within an IV framework where duration models are infeasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use linear-probability models including art-unit-by-application-year fixed effects to control for the fact that later applicants had less time to go public. Acknowledge limitations and justify model choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measuring collateralization and loans using patent assets
rubrics_metrics.description: When studying loans collateralized by patents or applications, recognize that lenders accept bundles of intangible assets and sometimes rejected applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure probability that a startup pledges its application as collateral and compare probabilities for approved vs rejected applications. Exclude VC-backed firms in robustness checks to assess independent effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness to examiner workload and other suggested controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Test whether including controls such as examiner workload at assignment affects the instrument coefficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include suggested reviewer-supplied robustness tests (e.g., workload) and report that main coefficient remains stable if instrument is valid.
